llm.summary: This skill does what it says: it lets a user check and control a Wyze robot vacuum, with disclosed use of Wyze credentials and tokens.

dimensions.detail: Use of WYZE_EMAIL, WYZE_KEY_ID, WYZE_API_KEY, WYZE_ENV, and cached tokens is disclosed and proportionate for authenticated Wyze device control.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup installs wyze-node from npm and package.json uses a caret dependency range, so installs are not fully reproducible and should be reviewed before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrow and user-directed; the skill warns that start should only run on a clear request and requires a vacuum name when multiple devices match.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script creates or uses a token directory and reuses cached Wyze authentication, but this is disclosed and limited to the integration purpose; no services, hooks, backdoors, or background workers were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose, CLI commands, and script behavior align: status reads vacuum state, while start, pause, and dock call the corresponding Wyze vacuum APIs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that this skill can use your Wyze API credentials and cached login to control a physical vacuum. Review the npm dependency, prefer a pinned version or lockfile, and only allow state-changing commands like start, pause, or dock when you explicitly ask for them.
llm.findings:
[YR4] expected: The matched text is the normal skill description about checking and controlling a robot vacuum; I found no tool spoofing, prompt override, exploit instruction, or malicious metadata behavior in the artifact.
[LP3] expected: The skill does use environment-backed Wyze credentials and cached authentication, but those are disclosed and necessary for the stated device-control purpose; the lack of a finer manifest permission boundary is a caution, not enough by itself for Review.
[SC1] unexpected: The unpinned npm dependency is a real supply-chain weakness, especially because the setup command installs wyze-node without a version, but there is no artifact evidence that the current skill ships malicious code or hides behavior.
[T08] unexpected: The SARIF dependency warning is supported by package.json and setup instructions; it warrants user caution and reproducible-install guidance but does not make the skill malicious or purpose-incoherent.
